title: Local-First Agentic Case Analysis Platform - Developer Handoff Blueprint for Federal Employee Suitability, Fitness, and National-Security Eligibility
summary: Source architecture paper proposing a local-first, bounded-agentic case-analysis platform for federal suitability, fitness, PIV, and SEAD-4 adjudication support; input to this project, not its output.

notes:
Manifest declared DOC at precedence 11 - accepted as authoritative and correct. Heuristics alone would have pulled toward SPEC (endpoint/contract tables, JSON schemas, state models, SLO-ish success criteria) and PRD (mission, in/out of scope, functional and non-functional success criteria), but the manifest classification is right for a different reason than signal strength: this document is the INPUT to the project, not its output. Per CLAUDE.md this is the LOWEST-precedence source in the ingest, and wherever it conflicts with docs/DECISIONS.md, DECISIONS.md wins. That is a project rule, not a preference. Downstream synthesis must treat every proposal in this file as CONTEXT ONLY - never as a requirement, constraint, or locked decision.

KNOWN DIVERGENCES - flag as conflicts, do NOT adopt: (1) Blueprint carries Neo4j forward as an optional component (sections 4.1, 15.2); ADR-006 declines a graph database in any milestone until evidence demands one. (2) Blueprint proposes a Streamlit case selector, run console, evidence viewer, and JSON export UI (Executive Summary and section 4.1.2); ADR-005 declines any UI in Milestone 1. (3) Blueprint requires a strict offline deterministic run profile that blocks all egress and replays recorded model fixtures or uses a local development model (sections 3.1, 12.7, and Executive Summary); ADR-009 declines it - there is no fixture provider and no local LLM server. (4) Blueprint recommends LangGraph by criteria comparison (sections 9.2-9.3); ADR-012 reached the same answer but by bake-off rather than paper comparison, and blueprint section 9.2 evaluates AutoGen and Semantic Kernel as live options when both moved to maintenance mode in April 2026 - the comparison table is stale and must not be cited as current. (5) Blueprint names Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 as the single model (Working assumptions, section 8.8); the current verified tier mapping is Sonnet 4.6 for ireports-orchestrator, Sonnet 5 for ireports-thinking, Haiku 4.5 for ireports-fast. Blueprint also predates the LiteLLM offline stub being dropped.

UNIQUE CONTRIBUTIONS worth extracting as context - nothing in the higher-precedence sources supersedes these: (a) Section 8.5 loop limits and termination, specifically the no-progress detector and duplicate-query detector alongside max model calls (3-5), max tool calls (8-12), max evidence count, token and wall-clock ceilings, required terminal tool, cancellation support, and the rule that a budget manager must emit incomplete_due_to_budget rather than silently omit work. (b) Section 8.2 state model - RunState carries identifiers and typed record IDs (structured_fact_ids, evidence_snapshot_ids, specialist_result_ids, proposed_finding_ids) rather than accumulated copies; large evidence text stays in the evidence store and is referenced by ID, which is both a token-cost and a sensitive-content-propagation control. (c) Section 2.1 on why authority routing is essential - suitability, fitness, PIV credentialing, and national-security eligibility are distinct authorities that must not collapse into one generic assessment. (d) Section 9.4 framework proof-of-concept scorecard dimensions - lines of framework-specific code, serialized state size, cold-start time and image size, resume correctness, ability to enforce budgets and tool allowlists, ease of inspecting and replaying state, test determinism, dependency and vulnerability footprint, developer comprehension after a two-hour onboarding exercise. (e) Section 10.1 contract versioning - semantic contract versions independent of application releases, validated at every boundary, published as JSON Schema with examples, breaking changes requiring a new major version and a compatibility plan. Section 8.4's tool allowlist and prohibited-tool list (no shell, generic HTTP, unrestricted filesystem, generic SQL, arbitrary Python, cross-case vector search, email, or direct ASAP delivery) is also unsuperseded and worth carrying.
